chapter: Trumpet styles and early New Orleans scene
title: Trumpet styles: Buddy Petit, Rene, Ricard, Chris Kelly
summary: Punch describes Petit's clean tone, Rene's high notes and Kelly's plunger work.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Well, let me get out my little notebook again, Punch, and we'll go back and I'll ask you about some of the different people and bands you work with, stuff like that. I wanted to ask you more about the different styles of the trumpet players they had here. Like, how would you describe Buddy Petit's style?

Well, I'm telling you, he had a wonderful style of playing at home. He wasn't a high note man, but he was, he had a wonderful tone and played everything clean. Real clean trumpet player. He was. Rene, he was a high note man. He went up in the air all the time. Ricard was turning out to be a nice trumpet player too until he got hype. Ricard was getting all right. What about Chris Kelly?
